introHeroTitle: Explore Canada's ocean data on one map
introHeroText: Temperature, salinity, currents, marine life and more, measured around Canada by scientists, governments and communities. Free to explore and download.
introShowcase_trajectory_body: Trace a glider, ship or drifter and every measurement along its path.
introShowcase_gridded_body: Show a model or satellite grid, then step through time and depth.
introShowcase_coverage_body: Chart data over time and spot the gaps.
introShowcase_nonna_body: Detailed seafloor depths from the Canadian Hydrographic Service's NONNA soundings.
introFeature_explore_body: Darker means more data. Click anywhere to see what was measured.
introFeature_search_body: Search by keyword, or filter by variable, time and place.
introFeature_download_body: Download it, or open it at its source.
introTipsText: Tips appear as you explore. Look for the <icon/> button when one is waiting.
introReopenText: Reopen this window with the <icon/> button beside the title.
tipInfoFeedback: Something not working, or have an idea? We read every message.
introSources: Data comes from ERDDAP™ servers run by CIOOS and its partners, and from OBIS (Ocean Biodiversity Information System).
tip_whatsHere: <add/> adds a dataset to your selection. It stays as you pan and filter, so you can gather datasets from several clicks before downloading.
tip_inView: Only want what's on screen? The In view button beside the dataset count keeps just the datasets in the map view.
tip_timeCoverage: Not sure which dates to pick? Time coverage in the top bar charts the data over time.
tip_speciesName: Looking for a species? In Filters, Scientific Name also finds common names, like “killer whale”.
tip_exclude: Filters can leave things out too: <exclude/> at the end of an option's row excludes it, like a platform type or a data portal you don't want.
tip_matchAll: Several ocean variables picked? Only datasets measuring all of them are shown. Turn off “Includes all selected” to see any of them.
tip_realtime: Want live data? The Real-time button beside the dataset count keeps only datasets still sending data at the last catalogue update.
tip_showData: Show data plots a feature's measurements, or lists them in a table, so you can check them before downloading.
tip_trajectory: In the legend's Trajectories group, step the date to see where each platform was that day. The menu beside Track sets how much of its path is drawn behind it.
tip_griddapWms: Turn on Show on map to draw a gridded dataset, then pick a variable and step through time and depth.
tip_filtersCutDownload: Your time, depth and area filters also cut the download: narrow them to get smaller files with only the data you need.
tip_directLinks: No email needed: the Download window's dataset list gives each dataset's query to its source, catalogue record, licence and citation.
tip_shareLink: The page address saves your view, filters, area and open dataset. Copy it to share, or bookmark it.

downloadModalSubtitleText: Review your selection, then receive it as a prepared archive by email or download it directly from the source.
downloadPackageFormatTooltipText: The emailed package, the Python script and the ERDDAP direct links take these formats. The package clips CSV, Parquet, ODV and NetCDF (CF) to a drawn polygon; ERDDAP's other file types come as ERDDAP writes them, over the polygon's bounding box. OBIS publishes occurrences only as a table, so OBIS datasets come as CSV or Parquet; OBIS direct links are always the dataset's Darwin Core Archive.
downloadRememberEmailLabel: Remember my email on this device
downloadEmailNotice: We use your email only to send you this download, and delete it 7 days after the download is processed, keeping just its domain (such as uvic.ca) for usage statistics.
downloadLinkLifetime_one: The emailed link works for {{count}} day, then the file is deleted.
downloadLinkLifetime_other: The emailed link works for {{count}} days, then the file is deleted.
privacyModalSubtitle: What this site keeps, what leaves your browser, and why.
privacy_device_title: Saved in your browser, not by us
privacy_device_body: This site sets no cookies. Your browser keeps a few settings for it on this device: your language, map layers, depth colours and projection, how the dataset list is displayed, which tips you've seen, whether you've closed the About window, and your email address if you ask it to be remembered. They are never sent to us. Clearing this site's data in your browser erases them.
privacy_email_body: Used only to send you the download link, or to tell you it failed. The message goes out through Google's Gmail service (<google>Google's privacy policy</google>). We delete the address from our download records 7 days after your download is processed. Only its domain (the part after the @, such as uvic.ca) is kept, to count downloads by institution.
privacy_errors_body: When something breaks, a report of what failed and on which page goes to Sentry, a service based in the United States (<sentry>Sentry's privacy policy</sentry>). It does not include your IP address or your email address. Feedback you send with the feedback button goes there too, with your email address only if you choose to give it.
privacy_analytics_body: We count visits with Plausible, run by CIOOS. It uses no cookies and keeps no personal information, only totals such as pages viewed, which site you came from, and how many download requests are submitted (with the number of datasets and the language, never your email address).
privacy_map_body: Your browser loads map backgrounds directly from their providers (EMODnet, OpenFreeMap and, for satellite imagery, Esri). Like any website, they see your IP address and which part of the map you are viewing. Seafloor depths come through our server from the Canadian Hydrographic Service (NONNA) and GEBCO, through the UK's CEDA archive: they see the area or the clicked point, never your IP address.
privacy_regions_body: When you type three or more characters in the filter search, your browser also sends what you typed to Natural Resources Canada's geographical names service to find matching places, even if you are not looking for one. Like any website, it sees your IP address (<nrcan>NRCan's privacy notice</nrcan>).
privacy_rights_body: To ask what we hold about you, or to have it corrected or deleted, see the <guidelines>CIOOS privacy guidelines</guidelines>.

selectionHelp_add_body: Click the + beside a dataset's title in the list. You can also add one straight from the map: click a point or a cell and use “Add this dataset to the selection” on the card that opens. Either way the count at the bottom of the list goes up.
selectionHelp_remove_title: Remove one, or change your mind later
selectionHelp_remove_body: A selected dataset shows a filled tick instead of the +. Click it again to take it out. The selection survives panning, filtering and searching, so you can gather datasets across several map clicks, and the Download window lets you untick anything before you submit.
selectionHelp_grid_body: Gridded (griddap) datasets are catalogued here but not served by the CDE, so their selection control is disabled. Open the dataset to reach its ERDDAP™ server and take the data there, where you can subset it yourself.
selectionHelp_size_body: In the Download window every selected dataset is measured against your filters. Anything still larger than 1 GB can't be delivered as a prepared archive: it is unticked and marked with a red cross, and the direct source link listed beside the order is how you get it. Narrowing the time, depth or map area usually brings it back under the limit.
selectionHelp_filters_title: Your filters travel with the order
selectionHelp_filters_body: Time, depth and the drawn area are applied to the download, and each can be switched off in the Download window. Three exceptions: direct ERDDAP™ links use the bounding box of a drawn polygon rather than its exact shape, datasets with no depth variable ignore the depth filter, and OBIS records come as the full dataset snapshot.

legendHelp_observations_body: Hexagon colour and marker size count the same thing: days of data, meaning the distinct days on which anything was measured in that place.
legendHelp_markers_body: Zoomed in past level 7, profile and time-series datasets stop being cells and are drawn at the locations they were collected from.
legendHelp_trajectories_line_body: The path a moving platform followed. Tracks ignore the time filter and draw the trailing window below instead.
legendHelp_trajectories_trail_body: How much history is drawn before the selected date, up to one year.
legendHelp_trajectories_head_body: Where the platform was on the selected date (its last fix up to that day) and which way it was going. A trajectory that ended before the date, or went silent well before it, has no marker. Set the date with the field beside the marker or the rail underneath.
legendHelp_seafloor_source_body: CHS NONNA bathymetry, its 10 m grid. Shaded for relief; it appears once the map is zoomed in far enough to draw it.
legendHelp_seafloor_colours_body: By default the depths run from pale yellow in the shallows through green and teal to deep purple, and read the same with any colour vision. The palette button beside "Depth (m)" switches to the Canadian Hydrographic Service's own NONNA colours, red in the shallows through yellow and green to dark blue, which some forms of colour blindness cannot tell apart. Your choice is kept on this device.
legendHelp_seafloor_tool_body: The crosshair beside "Depth (m)" turns on depth reading. While it is on, the cursor becomes a crosshair, hover popups pause, and a click anywhere on the map reads the depth there instead of opening the datasets under it: the depth is pinned at that point and marked on the depth bar. Press Esc or the crosshair again to turn it off; switching off the seafloor layer turns it off too.
legendHelp_seafloor_reading_body: CHS NONNA's 10 m grid answers where it has a sounding, in metres below chart datum; "Elevation" marks ground above chart datum, which uncovers at low tide. Everywhere else, the global GEBCO 2026 grid (about 460 m) answers in metres below mean sea level; land shows no depth.
legendHelp_seafloor_navigation_body: Neither NONNA (CHS's non-navigational bathymetry) nor GEBCO is fit for navigation. Use official CHS nautical charts to navigate.
legendHelp_layers_griddap_body: The bounding box of each gridded (griddap) dataset matching your filters. Gridded data is continuous over its whole box, so there is nothing to count per cell. It is drawn as an outline, not a colour ramp.
legendHelp_layers_download_body: The CDE does not prepare downloads for gridded data. Open a dataset to reach its ERDDAP™ server.
legendHelp_observations_once_body: However many datasets sampled it. Two moorings and a glider all recording on 1 January are one day of data between them, not three.
legendHelp_observations_gaps_body: The count follows the real sampling calendar: a station visited every January contributes those days alone, not the years in between.
legendHelp_observations_why_body: Record counts mix three different units across our sources (measurements, occurrence records and position fixes), and some are estimated from a sampling rate rather than measured. A day means the same thing everywhere, so any two places can be compared.
legendHelp_markers_size_body: Marker size shows the same count as a hexagon's colour. A marker is at its smallest at or below the number shown beside the small circle and grows from there. Where every location holds the same count there is no ramp to show, so they are all drawn at one size.
legendHelp_markers_colour_body: Mooring, ship, glider, and so on. Only the platform types present in your current results are listed, so the key never promises a colour the map is not drawing.
legendHelp_markers_cells_body: Trajectory tracks and OBIS occurrences are swept into coverage hexagons at every zoom, so those hexagons stay on the map underneath the markers.
legendHelp_observations_hover_body: A cell's colour is a total. Point at one and its tooltip names what that total is made of.
legendHelp_observations_scale_title: Scaled to what is on screen
legendHelp_observations_scale_body: The scale is recalculated for the hexagons in view, so the same green means different amounts at different zooms.
